title: SEC6: No hardware streaming hash for TLS objects
description: The decision not to route TLS transcript-hash objects to hardware (rather than attempting to patch the Copy path) is sound. The root cause is architectural: hardware streaming state lives in an fd, which cannot be snapshot-copied. Any attempt to intercept wc_Sha256Copy and re-replay the transcript to a new hardware op would require buffering all data written so far — O(transcript) per object — and would be fragile against future wolfSSL Copy call sites. The correct fix is to leave transcript hash on software and only use hardware for one-shot or HMAC operations, which is what TLS-safe mode does.
